title: QBR - Sapphire Technologies - Health Check
summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage trends, cost overruns on peak traffic, p95 latency spikes during nightly batch jobs, and roadmap alignment for upcoming integration with on-prem VPC. Redwood recommended KV caching and batching tweaks; discussed dedicated capacity and private deployment tradeoffs. Agreed action items to share cost breakdown and schedule technical deep dive and benchmark run.
next_steps: Redwood to send QBR deck and token-level cost sheet by 2026-05-18
Schedule SE-led benchmark for nightly batch workload week of 2026-05-25
Customer to confirm security contact for Private eval by 2026-05-20

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-15
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Gomez (Redwood SE), Karen Liu (Sapphire - Head of ML), Ravi Prakash (Sapphire - Platform), Sam Ortega (Sapphire - CTO)

Auto-generated Summary: quick QBR/check-in, usage up 28% QoQ, costs higher on peak windows, p95 spikes during nightly jobs; discuss Dedicated & Private for stabilizing latency and cost predictability.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everybody, thanks for joining, um this is maya from Redwood, with Ethan our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Karen: good, thanks. busy end of quarter but excited to go through the qbr.
[00:15] Sam: morning all, yes let's run through the numbers.
[00:20] Ethan: thanks, quick agenda, usage/cost trends, reliability/latency, security items and roadmap alignment, then action items.

[02:05] Maya: first slide, usage is up about 28 percent q over q, tokens/month went from ~1.2B to 1.54B, a lot of that is our nightly summarization and a new chat feature. sounded right from your side, karen?
[02:20] Karen: yeah that's correct. the summarization jobs in particular ballooned after we added multi-doc context. it's mostly off-peak but it's big in token count.

[04:10] Ravi: quick flag, our bill spiked last month by nearly 40 percent, we saw a p99 on cost per token for one week. can you help explain where that's coming from?
[04:25] Maya: yeah so what we saw in the logs is there's a small subset of requests that were hitting long contexts and not using cache - so no prefix caching, and also gamma clientes were sending high temperature leading to wider generations. Ethan, do you want to add?
[04:40] Ethan: sure. two things: one, the KV cash (sic) wasn't being hit for the nightly pipeline because the job uses unique doc ids, so no reuse. two, batching settings are conservative on your project to prioritize latency; that increases per-token cost. if we relax batching thresholds for your async summarization, we can drive down unit cost significantly.

[06:00] Karen: can you quantify that? like how much savings?
[06:10] Ethan: ballpark, for the night summarization if we enable 300ms max wait for batching and use prefix caching for repeated doc chunks we'd expect 20-30 percent token cost reduction on that workload. overall account-level might drop 10-15 percent.

[08:30] Sam: what about latency SLOs? our product team is concerned if we tune batching more we'll get user-perceived lag.
[08:40] Maya: great question. tradeoffs are per-route; we can route interactive chat to low-latency hosted nodes and route batch summarization to dedicated/batched pools. that gives you both low p50 for chat and lower average cost for batch.

[10:05] Ravi: we've been talking internally about Redwood Dedicated given our growth. can you remind us the main benefits vs hosted?
[10:15] Ethan: dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput and lower variance on p95, plus data isolation. cost model is commit/flat monthly vs pay-as-you-go hosted. also easier to pin a model variant and quantization profile.

[12:30] Karen: and Private (VPC/on-prem)? we have regulatory needs for some docs; is that a path here?
[12:40] Maya: yes private gives you a customer-managed control plane or on-prem option. integrates with your KMS/HSM for key management, plus audit logs. there is onboarding work and network setup; we typically run a pilot in a VPC first.

[14:20] Ravi: security list - we need SOC2 type II evidence, SSO/SAML setup, RBAC config screenshots, and audit logs retention policies; can you compile that?
[14:30] Maya: absolutely, we'll send our security pack and SOC2 attestation. Ethan will also share example audit log exports.

[16:50] Karen: reliability - we've had a couple p95 spikes around 03:30 UTC last two weeks, coincident with your autoscaling events. any recommended mitigations?
[17:05] Ethan: the spikes align with bursty queuing when autoscaler spins up new nodes; recommended: configure burst capacity and keep warm pools for the window, and set fallback model variants (smaller quantized models) for degraded capacity. also consider KV cache for prefix reuse.

[18:45] Sam: curious about quantization - how much impact on latency/cost vs quality? we saw some hallucination noise in previous tests.

[19:00] Ethan: quantization can reduce memory and inference time significantly; 4-bit/8-bit depends on model. quality can be preserved with calibrations and eval prompt sets; we'd run a quick regression eval against your golden prompts before rollout.

[21:20] Maya: on the QBR recommendations: 1) enable prefix caching on nightly summarization, 2) relax batching for async jobs, 3) run a small Dedicated pilot for peak-week to measure p95 stabilization, 4) security pack delivery. those are the main items.

[23:10] Karen: sounds good. can you share the token-level cost breakdown? need to present to finance.
[23:20] Maya: yes we'll share the spreadsheet with token-level granularity and suggested changes to batching and cache - that's one of the action items.

[25:00] Ravi: for the Dedicated pilot, what's the sizing guidance? we average 800 qps at peak during business hours and about 2.5k async summarization jobs at night.

[25:15] Ethan: initial pilot: 4 reserved GPUs with burst policy and autoscale to 6 for peak. we'll simulate your 800 p50/p95 and nightly batch to produce expected utilization curves.

[27:40] Karen: given all that, timeline wise we'd like to have the pilot results before the renewal conversation in July. is that feasible?
[27:50] Maya: yes feasible. plan: benchmark week of 2026-05-25, pilot onboarding early June, run for 4 weeks, review mid-June so you have results for July renewal planning.

[30:05] Sam: one more thing - costs for retention. we store logs and embeddings; finance asked about retention tiers. can Redwood help with retention policies / cold storage?

[30:20] Ethan: yes we offer configurable retention and export to your S3 bucket or long-term cold storage. we can also purge vector indexes older than x days. we'll include retention config options in the cost sheet.

[32:00] Karen: security contact for private eval will be our security lead, sasha ng, cc'd later. she'll want network diagram and hardening steps.

[32:10] Maya: perfect, we'll include a checklist for the security review.

[34:40] Ravi: regarding the nightly job causing cache misses, a small engineering change on our side could key doc ids to canonical prefixes so cache hits happen; we'll plan that in the infra backlog.

[34:55] Karen: yes we'll prioritize that.

[36:30] Ethan: also a note on instrumentation: adding token-level tracing and latency tags per route will help us correlate spikes to model variants or infra events.

[38:00] Maya: any competitor pressures we should be aware of? karen, you mentioned the team experimenting with other hosted endpoints last quarter.

[38:12] Karen: yes small experiments with OpenAI for some newer models but we hit cost/latency tradeoffs; also evaluating Anthropic for safety features. not at scale though.

[40:05] Maya: okay good to know. we'll include comparative notes in the deck.

[41:20] Sam: ok let's recap the next steps, who owns what.

[41:30] Maya: recap: maya to send QBR deck + cost sheet by monday 05/18; ethan to schedule benchmark plan and run week of 05/25; karen to share example prompts and peak windows by 05/17; ravi to share infra diagram and firewall details by 05/20; customer security lead to confirm contact.

[42:15] Karen: yep we'll do that. quick note - transcription sometimes misses technical terms, saw KV cash in the notes :-)

[42:25] Ethan: ha yes we saw that, kv cache.

[44:00] Maya: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark and a separate security review. thanks for your time.

[44:15] Sam: thanks all.

[44:30] Meeting ended.
